title: 📰 AI news · November 16

items.title: Hackers planted a malicious Claude Code in Cursor's marketplace
items.text: Hackers stole a key from the contractor Fireworks AI and reached Cursor's internal systems. Two malicious copies of the Claude Code extension sat in the marketplace for 11 hours and tried to install hidden SSH access; up to 5,000 people requested them. If you run a bot or an AI agent, keys may sit in plain text in its activity history. Check today which keys stay in the history of your agents. Free guide «Protecting your computer, code and access»: send the word «protect» to the bot.

items.title: FBI: hackers use the AI tool ARTEX to break in
items.text: ARTEX is an open program where AI agents find weak spots on their own, break into systems and take data. From the first target to elevated access takes under three hours. If you have a site, bot or AI agent, similar automated tools can probe it. Check today which systems of your project are visible from the internet.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 paints pictures with code
items.text: The model writes a Python program that places hundreds of thousands of strokes on a virtual canvas. One photorealistic parking-garage scene took about 700,000 strokes. The program simulates bristles, wet paint and canvas texture.

items.title: Meituan opens LongCat-2.5 with 1.6 trillion parameters
items.text: The weights are on Hugging Face under the MIT license. About 48 billion parameters work on each step, and the model scored 88.4 on Terminal Bench. The sample deployment runs on 194 Huawei Ascend accelerators.

items.title: Runway opens Praxis-1, a video model that controls robots
items.text: The model looks at camera frames, reads a command and calculates the robot's movements. It scored 46.2 percent on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 leaderboard. Apache 2.0 license, code on GitHub, weights on Hugging Face.

items.title: ChatGPT gets a wallet for AI agents
items.text: Agents choose products and pay for them. At first only some ChatGPT Pro users in the US, aged 18 and up, get it; it works with Visa, Mastercard and American Express cards. There are no spending limits at launch; OpenAI promises to add them later.

items.title: Thinking Machines opens Inkling 2 Small weights
items.text: The model has 594 billion parameters, 17 billion active on each step, and takes text and images. The weights are on Hugging Face, as the company promised.

items.title: Starship returned from orbit into the tower's arms
items.text: The ship spent about 22.5 hours in space and made 14 orbits of Earth. On November 14 the tower's mechanical arms in Texas caught it. The booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico.

items.title: Vulcan rocket loses 40 Amazon Leo satellites
items.text: The failure happened about 10 minutes after liftoff on November 15. All 40 Amazon internet satellites were lost, and the cause has not been named.

items.title: Tesla opens orders for a personal Cybercab
items.text: The price is $29,990, plus a non-refundable $1,000 deposit and a $299 monthly Autonomy subscription. The car drives only inside Robotaxi zones in Texas and Florida; first deliveries in Austin are expected in December.

items.title: AO3 is back after 17 days offline over a breach
items.text: The fanfiction archive reopened on November 15, no data was deleted, and some features are still off. The team cannot rule out that the user database was accessed. If you have an AO3 account, change that password and everywhere you reused it.

items.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million
items.text: Facebook for Android read the phone gallery through one broad permission, with the feature on by default. About 20 million users in Italy were affected. Check which apps on your phone can see your whole gallery.

items.title: Coinone: support chat data leaked via contractor
items.text: An attacker breached the contractor running the exchange's support and took what customers wrote in chats, including passwords and ID numbers. It concerns those who contacted support. If that is you, change your exchange password and anywhere it is reused.

items.title: Project Zero cuts disclosure deadline to 30 days
items.text: Google will publish bugs after a fixed deadline: 90 days now, 60 days from February 2027, 30 days from January 2028. The reason: AI sped up both finding bugs and building attacks. Turn on automatic updates on your phone and computer.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra helps a physicist with the Standard Model
items.text: In the first guest post on OpenAI's science blog, physicist Nathaniel Craig describes how Astra turned his strategy into a lattice construction and led the detailed proof. The result is a candidate that experts still need to check.

items.title: Grok Imagine images and video now live in Grok
items.text: Since November 14, images and videos are created right in the Grok app: open the chat and ask for a picture or a clip.

items.title: Musk: Starship V4 will be about 70 meters long
items.text: The next version will be roughly 40% longer and carry over 60% more propellant. It will have 9 engines, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines of the higher-thrust V4 version.

takeaway: Today's news is about access: keys get stolen through contractors, and AI agents speed up break-ins. Recommendation: check which keys sit in the history of your agents and close what does not need to be on the internet.
